questions.question: Who was responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**General Dyer.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jallianwala Bagh massacre**, also known as the **Amritsar massacre**, took place on **13 April 1919**.
 
• During the annual** Baishakhi festival** in Amritsar, Punjab, British India, a sizable and nonviolent gathering had convened at the Jallianwala Bagh to express **disapproval of the Rowlatt Act** and the apprehension of pro-independence activists **Saifuddin Kitchlew** and **Satyapal**.
 
• Temporary **Brigadier General Reginald E. H. Dyer** encircled the mass of unarmed civilians and ordered open fire in reaction to their public gathering.
 
• After the incident, **Rabindranath Tagore renounced his 'Knighthood".**
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi **gave up his title of** 'Kaiser-i-Hind'** and **withdrew the Satyagrah against Rowlatt Act.**

• **Rowlatt Act**:

 
 
• The Rowlatt Act, also known as the** Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919**, was enacted by the British government, prompting the Rowlatt Satyagraha. 
 
• On the advice of the **Sir Sidney Rowlatt** who **chaired Sedition Committee**, this act was passed. Despite the Indian members' unanimous opposition, the Imperial Legislative Council rushed this act through **in March 1919.**
 
• It gave the government broad powers to stifle political activity and allowed the** two-year imprisonment of political prisoners without charge or trial.**
 
• Gandhiji demanded that the Rowlatt Act be opposed nationally.

• She was a **publisher, political activist**, and** educator** from** India**.
 
• She was an **ardent member** of the fight for **Indian independence**, and she is well known for hosting the **Indian National flag** at the **Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay in 1942, during the Quit India Movement.**
 
• In the** Indian Independence Movement**, **Aruna Asaf Ali **played a significant role.
 
• After getting married to** Asaf Ali**, she joined the** Indian National Congress **and took part in the **Salt Satyagraha's public processions**.
 
• She was imprisoned in** 1931** in violation of the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**, which called for the release of all political prisoners, since she was accused of being a **wanderer.**
 
 
 
• **​Sucheta Kripalni - **
 
 
• **Sucheta Kriplani** was born on **June 25, 1908**.
 
• She joined **the freedom struggle** after completing her graduation and became a disciple of **Gandhiji**.
 
• In **1936** She married **JB Kriplani**.
 
• She also laid the **foundation of Women's wing of Congress** in **1940**.
 
• She handled underground **non-violent political activities** during the **freedom struggle**.
 
• She was appointed a member of the **constituent assembly** in **1946.**
 
• She sang** Vande Mataram** on **14th August 1947** in the opening session of **parliament**.
 
• But due to ideological differences with Nehru, she along with her husband left congress after Independence.
 
• She formed a new party of her called** Kisan Majdoor Praja Party** and served as **MP** from** New Delhi**.
 
• But in** 1957 **she rejoined the congress and in **1963** became the **Chief Minister** of **Uttar Pradesh**.

questions.question: The __________ Commission was set up to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e__** Hunter**__

**Jallianwala Bagh massacre:**

 
• **On 13th April,** a large crowd of people from neighbouring villages, unaware of the prohibitory orders in the** Amritsar** gathered in the **Jallianwala Bagh.**
 
• **Brigadier-General Dyer** arrived on the scene with his men and he gave the orders to his men to fire on the unarmed crowd killing more than 1000 unarmed men, women, and children.
 
• The government formed a committee of inquiry to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh shooting named **Disorders Inquiry Committee**.which is known as **Hunter Commission** after the** name of chairman, Lord William Hunter.**
 
• The Committee submitted its report in **1920** but they did not impose any penalty or disciplinary action against General Dyer.

questions.question: The Sanchi monument is one of the most well-preserved Indian Buddhist stupas located in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is "__**Madhya Pradesh**__".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **Sanchi Stupa is a** historic site of **Sanchi in Madhya Pradesh **state, India.
 
• It is one of the **oldest** **Buddhist monuments** in the country and the **largest stupa at the site.**
 
• The Great Stupa (also called stupa no. 1) was originally built in the** 3rd century BCE** by the **Mauryan emperor Ashoka **and is believed to house the ashes of the **Buddha**.
 
• The building is** 120 feet (37 meters) **wide and** 54 feet (17 meters)** high.
 
• The Great Stupa and Sanchi’s other Buddhist monuments were collectively designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1989.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The central structure consists of a **hemispherical** **dome** on a base, with a deep chamber within.
 
• The dome symbolizes, among other things, the dome of **heaven** **enclosing the earth.**
 
• It is surmounted by a squared railing that can be said to represent the world mountain.
 
• A central pillar (Vashti) symbolizes the cosmic axis and supports a triple umbrella structure, which is held to represent the **Three Jewels of Buddhism**—**the Buddha**, **the dharma (doctrine)**, and **the sangha (community).**
 
• A circular terrace (Medhi), enclosed by a railing, surrounds the dome, on which the faithful are to circumambulate in a **clockwise** **direction**.
 
• The entire structure is enclosed by a low wall (vedika), which is punctuated at the four **cardinal** **points** by **toranas** (ceremonial gateways).

• Under Gokhale’s leadership, the Congress strongly condemned the partition and emphasized the need for **Swadeshi (self-reliance) and boycott of British goods**.
 
• Gokhale's vision during the session laid the foundation for future strategies in India's freedom movement, blending moderation with a growing emphasis on self-reliance.

• This meant that Muslim electorates were given the right to vote in both general and separate Muslim electorates.
 
 
 
• **Repartition of Bengal and Punjab:**
 
 
• **​**The pact outlined a **re-distribution of seats in Bengal and Punjab** based on population and community composition.
 
• This aimed to provide a more accurate representation of the communities living in these areas.
 
 
 
• **Decentralization:**
 
 
• **​**The Lucknow Pact called for the **decentralization of power, allowing provinces greater autonomy.**
 
• **This meant a significant shift towards self-governance.**
 
 
 
• **Unity Among Leaders:**
 
 
• **​**The Lucknow Pact was a** landmark moment in Indian history, as it signified a rare moment of unity among Indian leaders.**
 
• Both the Indian **National Congress and the Muslim League came together to make a joint demand for greater autonomy from British rule.**
 
• **This set the tone for future collaborations and marked a pivotal moment in India's freedom struggle.**

questions.question: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress when India won its freedom in the year 1947?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**J. B. Kripalani.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **J. B. Kripalani**__

 __
 
• ​He was the** president of the Indian National Congress in 1947.**
 
• He was popularly known as **Acharya Kripalani.**
 
• From 1920 to 1927, he worked as the principal of **Gujarat Vidyapeeth which was an educational institution set up by Gandhi.** There he earned the **Epithet 'Acharya'.**
 
• He was elected the **General Secretary of the Indian National Congress (INC) in 1934 and continued to serve in the post for a long time till 1945.**
 
• In November** 1946**, he was elected the **President of the Congress Party.​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ​**Jawaharlal Nehru**__

 __
 
• ​He was the **first Prime minister of India.**
 
• He was also** India's longest-serving prime minister **(15 Aug 1947 to 27 May 1964)
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru along with Srinivasa Iyengar and Subhash Chandra Bose founded the Independence for India League in the year 1928 which put forth the demand for complete independence.
 
• **Books were written by him**: The Discovery of India, Letters from a Father to his Daughter, Glimpses of World History etc.
 
 
 
• **​Vallabhbhai Patel**__
 __
 
• ​He was popularly known as **Sardar Patel, Bismarck of India, Iron Man of India, Strong Man.**
 
• He was the **first Deputy Prime Minister of India.**
 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's statue or known as the Statue of Unity is situated in Gujarat India. It is the world's tallest statue standing at a height of 182 meters.
 
• Indian National Trade Union Congress was founded in 1947 by him.
 
• In 1928, he led the peasant movement in Bardoli, a taluka in Gujarat, against the enhancement of land revenue.
 
 
 
• ​**Abul Kalam Azad**__
 
 
• ​He was an **Indian independence activist, Islamic theologian, writer, and senior leader of the Indian National Congress.**
 
• **He was the First Education Minister in the Indian government.**
 
• He is commonly remembered as **Maulana Azad.**
 
• His contribution to establishing the education foundation in India is recognised by celebrating his birthday as National Education Day across India.
